source.title: On the Inductive Bias of Neural Tangent Kernels

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the relevant findings.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes NTK function-space properties and reports numerical measurements of representation distances under image deformations. Those measurements bear on V7's generalization-measure topic only indirectly; the paper does not measure training-to-test gaps or any of V1–V8's specified outcomes. Its own stability findings concern deformation stability, a distinct construct, so the closest relation is a conceptual test of adjacent inductive-bias properties rather than a test of the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a numerical comparison of NTK and CKN kernel-map distances for digit images and deformations, but it does not report any result about natural-label test error, memorization, the training-to-test gap, or a measure tracking that gap. The Figure 1 distances are included as claim-adjacent measurement results under fits_no_version; theoretical discussion of approximation and stability is not a result for a mapped version.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes NTK function spaces and measures distances between image representations under deformations. Neither these distances nor its approximation and stability theorems test V1–V8. Input-deformation stability is distinct from V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate, with approximation results specifically established for two-layer ReLU NTKs. The authors establish weaker smoothness but better approximation properties than the compared ReLU kernels, and a weaker deformation-stability guarantee for convolutional NTKs. They caution that finite-width networks need not inherit the limiting RKHS's stability and that lazy training does not capture feature learning.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes limiting neural tangent kernels and their RKHS properties, with a numerical representation-distance comparison against a convolutional kernel network; it does not use the original generalization-gap interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Kernel choice (NTK versus CKN) changes the reported relative distances and their growth for small deformations; deformation size varies across the plotted conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: For the tested two-layer convolutional kernels, representation distance grows faster under small image deformations for NTK than CKN; relative distances are generally larger for NTK.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On the tested Infinite MNIST images, the convolutional NTK representation is less smooth under input deformations than the corresponding arc-cosine degree-1 CKN representation.

record.problems: The numerical results are presented in Figure 1 without numerical values in the text. The paper studies kernel-map stability rather than natural-label generalization gaps; its analysis is in the infinite-width NTK regime and does not establish that finite networks share the same properties.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant results were left out. The paper's theoretical statements about smoothness, approximation rates, and deformation-stability bounds do not measure the training-to-test gap or any mapped version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Held-out performance of convolutional versus fully connected networks, including local connectivity and initialization effects.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, configurations, and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, measured generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's tests/T2 classification with discusses/T6. Theoretical approximation quality and deformation stability do not establish held-out classification performance or any mapped generalization effect.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label held-out performance is measured.
